purpose: SOUTH WALK 3-frame animation (walk_south_1/2/3.png) + SOUTH IDLE (south_idle.png, frame 1 reused per explicit instruction).
processing: Non-generative only -- no AI redraw/regeneration. Two deterministic steps per source image: (1) white-background unblend, (2) landmark-based scale+anchor onto the existing shared 700x920 boss canvas.

step1_white_unblend.problem: Each source PNG already carried a real alpha channel, but it was reconstructed by flattening over a white background and taking 'distance from white' as alpha, WITHOUT un-premultiplying the RGB -- so edge/antialiased pixels kept their white-blended color. Verified by bucketing edge pixels (alpha in (3,250)) by alpha value: mean brightness rose monotonically from ~98 at alpha 200-250 up to ~230 at alpha 3-30, i.e. the more transparent a pixel was, the whiter its stored RGB was -- the signature of an unblended white-bg composite, and would show as a visible white/gray fringe once composited over any non-white game background.
step1_white_unblend.formula: For every pixel with alpha>0: true_color F = clip((RGB_stored - (1-alpha/255)*255) / (alpha/255), 0, 255); alpha itself is kept as-is (it was already a reasonable opacity matte, just paired with the wrong un-premultiplied RGB). Pixels with alpha==0 are zeroed (RGB=0) since they are fully transparent regardless. This is the standard, deterministic 'un-premultiply against a known background color' formula (assumes background = pure white, matching the source), not a synthesized/AI value.
step1_white_unblend.verification: Re-bucketed the same edge pixels by alpha after the correction: mean brightness became roughly flat across the mid/high alpha ranges (~50-90) instead of climbing toward white at low alpha; visually confirmed via composites over dark-navy and mid-gray test backgrounds (see wingzoom crop in the session) that wing-tip/feather edges show no white or gray halo.

step2_landmark_scale_anchor.reference: The pre-existing walk_south_1.png/walk_south_2.png (both already living on the shared 700x920 canvas) were measured the same way: head_top_y found by scanning alpha>10 within columns x > 35% of image width (excludes the wing, which is entirely left-of-center in this pose) for the topmost row, head_center_x from the midpoint of that topmost row's opaque span, feet_bottom_y from the single lowest opaque row overall (a foot/claw tip). Existing values: walk_south_1 head_top_y=132 head_center_x=366.0 feet_bottom_y=899; walk_south_2 head_top_y=127 head_center_x=365.5 feet_bottom_y=899.

targets_derived_from_reference.note: TARGET_BODY_SPAN_PX is the average of the two existing frames' own (feet_bottom_y - head_top_y), i.e. this batch matches the EXISTING SOUTH WALK images' own on-canvas body size, not an arbitrary new value -- per the explicit instruction to keep the pre-existing apparent size.

step2_landmark_scale_anchor.scale_formula: scale = TARGET_BODY_SPAN_PX / native_body_span (per-image, since the 3 sources are not pixel-identical in framing).
step2_landmark_scale_anchor.placement_formula: After resizing by `scale`: paste_x = round(TARGET_CENTER_X - head_center_x*scale); paste_y = round(TARGET_FEET_BOTTOM_Y - feet_bottom_y*scale); pasted onto a fresh transparent 700x920 canvas.

verification_on_final_canvas.note: All three land within 2px of the TARGET values and of each other -- no per-frame jump in size, position, or foot anchor. (A 0.35-width head-detection threshold mis-measured frame3's re-verification by catching a raised wing-feather tip near that boundary at x~244; re-run with a >=0.40-width threshold, matching how the ORIGINAL placement math for that frame was computed, correctly reads head_center_x=365.0 -- confirmed visually as well, no side-to-side jump between frames.)

south_idle_reuse: south_idle.png is a byte-identical copy of the final walk_south_1.png canvas (frame 1), per explicit instruction that SOUTH IDLE and SOUTH WALK FRAME 1 share the exact same image/scale/anchor -- guarantees zero size or position jump on any IDLE<->WALK transition.
in_game_scale: All four files (south_idle, walk_south_1/2/3) continue to use the existing SOUTH_WALK_SCALE (1.10) render-time multiplier applied uniformly in drawBoss() -- unchanged from before this batch, and applied identically to all four so relative proportions are preserved.
animation_wiring: bossFrameName() now cycles walk_south_1 -> walk_south_2 -> walk_south_3 -> walk_south_1... via `Math.floor(now / WALK_FRAME_PERIOD_MS) % 3` while boss.moving and facing south; WALK_FRAME_PERIOD_MS unchanged (natural walking cadence, not a fast flicker).
dark_phase_exclusion: DARK PHASE never draws south_idle/walk_south_* (or any other normal battle sprite) -- see drawBossDarkPhase() in game.js, which only ever draws the dedicated dark_phase.png / red-eye VFX.
